= CHERIoT memory subsystem: design architecture
:toc: left
:toclevels: 2
:sectnums:
:imagesdir: figures

This doc explains how the CHERIoT memory subsystem (`cheriot_mem_sys`) works, for a reader who has
never seen it. It covers the capability tag path in depth: the path that stores and returns the
one-bit "tag" that marks a 64-bit value as a valid capability. Its two main blocks are the core's
tag filter and the RMW (read-modify-write) filter. Section 2 explains them from zero, with worked
examples; section 3 holds the requirements (the vplan) of the whole subsystem, the assumptions DV
makes and the questions for the designers; section 4 holds the risks and findings of the revocation
flow. How the requirements are checked (three checkers: tag path, meta access,
revocation engine; contracts C1 to C7; open decisions Dn) is in the
xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc[FPV testbench architecture]; the testpoints that
translate each requirement into checks, cases and edge cases are in the
xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc[FPV testplan].

*For the designers:* this doc is DV's reading of your design. The requirements say how we
understand each block, the assumptions what we take for granted about its inputs and neighbours,
and the questions what we need clarified to verify it; all three are in section 3. Please tell us
by ID (`REQ_*`, `An`, `Qn`) where we are wrong, and answer the questions (designer questions).
The Source column marks every requirement and assumption that rests on DV's reading or on the RTL
rather than on the spec text; each of those has a question too (Source legend).

== Overview

=== Block diagram

*Rule:* every core data access passes through the tag filter; accesses that need a tag also go
down the tag path to the meta SRAM.

.The capability tag path through `cheriot_mem_sys`
image::cheriot_mem_sys_design_arch_figures.svg#fig1[Tag path block diagram,align=center,width=810,height=816]

[cols="1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Step |What happens

|1 |The Ibex core sends a data access on `cored_tl_d`, with a tag bit beside it.
|2 |The tag filter forwards the data half unchanged to `xbar_main` on `cored_tl_h`, which reaches
the SRAM, the NVM (non-volatile memory) and the peripherals.
|3 |If the access needs a tag, the tag filter also sends a tag request on its meta port.
|4 |The 2:1 tag arbiter (`cheriot_socket_m1`) merges it with the tag requests of the TBRE
(background revocation engine), which has a tag filter of its own.
|5 |The tag clear squash passes the core's tag requests on unchanged. It turns a TBRE tag clear that
a core write overtook into a read (tag sharing).
|6 |The RMW filter turns the tag request into whole-word reads and writes.
|7 |The access checker lets only legal tag-region accesses through.
|8 |`tlul_socket_m1` arbitrates them with three other checked streams onto the one meta SRAM port.
|===

'''

=== Memories and address map

*Rule:* the tag path reaches only the meta SRAM, and only through `meta_sram_tl`; every other
memory sits behind `xbar_main`.

.`cheriot_mem_sys` in Earl Grey: its ports, the memories behind `xbar_main` and the meta SRAM
image::cheriot_mem_sys_design_arch_figures.svg#fig2["cheriot_mem_sys ports, memories and address map",align=center,width=900,height=1020]

[cols="1,5",options="header"]
|===
|Point |What the figure shows

|Core data path |Data accesses go from the Ibex core through the tag filter, in on `cored_tl_d` and
out on `cored_tl_h`, to `xbar_main`. Instruction fetches do not pass the subsystem: `cored_tl_d`
carries "Core data accesses with the capability tag support" ([ToO] port table).
|Memories that hold capabilities |Main SRAM, Secondary SRAM and NVM (yellow). The two SRAMs form
one tagged region: [ToO] counts "192 KiB main SRAM at `0x1000_0000`{empty}", which in Earl Grey is
the 128 KiB main SRAM plus the "64 KiB Secondary SRAM" ([EG]). R6 asks for the name to be fixed.
|ROM |192 KiB, with no tags: it is not a tagged region.
|Meta SRAM |38 KiB, not on `xbar_main`: "the RAM interface is only reachable from
`meta_sram_tl`{empty}" ([ToO] Meta SRAM Address Map).
|Four checked streams |The core's TRVK bitmap reads (`corerevbm_tl`), the tag path, the TBRE's
TRVK filter and the bitmap window (`revbm_tl_d`) each pass "an access checker parameterized with
the region it owns"; "A `tlul_socket_m1` arbitrates the four checked streams onto
`meta_sram_tl`{empty}" ([ToO] Access Checkers, Arbitration).
|TBRE |Reads memory over `tbre_tl_h`, a "Read-only port of the revocation engine towards the
memories holding capabilities" ([ToO] port table). Its tag filter joins the tag path at the 2:1
tag arbiter; the dashed line up to the squash is its watch of core writes and its clears
(revocation).
|CSRs |Software starts and follows a sweep through the registers on `regs_tl_d` (the two-way dashed line to the engine): "A write of 1 to `TBRE_START` starts a sweep over `TBRE_NUM_CAPS` capabilities
from `TBRE_BASE_ADDR`{empty}"; `TBRE_REGWEN`, `TBRE_STATUS` and `TBRE_EPOCH` report back ([ToO]
Revocation Engine).
|Debug SBA |"a crossbar host of its own and does not pass through the tag filter" ([ToO] System Bus Access): its writes leave tags as they were.
|Address map table |Addresses and sizes from [EG] and the [ToO] Meta SRAM Address Map. The split of
the 3 KiB SRAM tag region into main (`0x1100_8C00`-`0x1100_93FF`) and secondary
(`0x1100_9400`-`0x1100_97FF`) assumes the word and bit order asked in Q2.
|===

=== Scope and status

[cols="3,1,4",options="header"]
|===
|Section |Status |Holds

|How the tag path works (spec) |draft |background from zero, with the meta SRAM and revocation;
tag filter; 2:1 tag arbiter; RMW filter; sharing; an end-to-end example
|Requirements |draft |144 requirements with why each matters (the WTRC, revocation engine, registers and alert rows still for agreement); 16 assumptions; a trace of every [HJSON] feature and
countermeasure; 24 open questions for the designers (12 closed); testpoints in the testplan
|Open items |draft |11 open findings: R16 critical if confirmed, the rest minor
|Checker flow, open decisions, traceability |draft |moved to the xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc[TB architecture]
|===

* **In scope:** the core's tag filter, the one that answers the Ibex core through its fork and
  join; the 2:1 tag arbiter in front of the RMW filter; the RMW filter; and the path from them to
  the meta SRAM port. The meta SRAM access of all four requesters (access checkers, 4:1 arbiter,
  bitmap window) has requirements of its own, `REQ_META_*`.
* **Requirements, not yet explained here:** the TBRE with its own tag filter (`TagOnlyWrites`), its
  TRVK (tag revocation) filter, the core write watch and the tag clear squash (`REQ_TBRE_*`,
  checker 3); the WTRC for capability stores to the NVM (`REQ_WTRC_*`, checker 1); the registers
  and the alert (`REQ_REG_01`, `REQ_ALT_*`). Section 2 explains them only as background; the
  testplan gives each one's operating principles.
* **Out of scope:** what the memories do with a correct request (A11), and the blocks outside the
  subsystem: the Ibex core with its own TRVK filter, `xbar_main`, the debug module.

== Requirements

=== Overview

A requirement is one testable sentence of what the design must do, taken from the spec. Each has an
ID that never changes, so checks, results and discussions can point at it. "Why it matters" says
what would go wrong if the design broke it.

[cols="2,1,4",options="header"]
|===
|Group |Count |Checker

|`REQ_TF_*` tag filter |25 |1 tag path
|`REQ_ARB_*` 2:1 tag arbiter |11 |1 tag path
|`REQ_RMW_*` RMW filter |17 |1 tag path
|`REQ_TAG_*` tag path end to end |11 |1 tag path (`_07`, `_08`, `_10`); 2 meta access (`_05`, `_06`, `_11`); by composition (`_01`-`_04`, `_09`)
|`REQ_META_*` meta SRAM access |16 |2 meta access
|`REQ_WTRC_*` capability stores to the NVM |14 |1 tag path
|`REQ_TBRE_*` revocation engine |43 |3 revocation; by composition (`_38`, `_39`)
|`REQ_REG_*`, `REQ_ALT_*` registers and alert |7 |3 revocation (`REG_01`, `REG_02`, `ALT_01`-`_03`); by
composition (`ALT_04`, `ALT_05`)
|===

* The WTRC, revocation engine and register groups are new drafts, for agreement.
* Each requirement is translated into testpoints, with its cases, edge cases and run, in the
  xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc[FPV testplan].
* Method is FPV for every row except the register rows whose Obligations name CSR testing
  (`csr`, `alert_test`; owner still to name), so the tables have no Method column. Obligations name the checks of
  the check plan; they read "to plan" until it is written.
* A requirement split into parts keeps its number with a letter (`REQ_TF_05a`, `REQ_TF_05b`). A
  removed ID is never reused: `REQ_RMW_12` was folded into `REQ_TAG_08`.
* Status is `planned`, `gap: Qn` where the requirement waits on a question for the designers
  (designer questions), or `out of scope` where only a core that breaks its own access order
  reaches it: the core is spec compliant, and what the design does then is a different verification
  task.
* [[requirements_source]]*Source* says where each requirement comes from, so the designers can see
  which rows to confirm:
** `spec`: the spec states it; the quote is in Spec ref. DV only restates it as a testable sentence.
** `DV reading`: the spec implies it but does not state it, or leaves a term open; this is DV's
   reading. Please confirm.
** `RTL (integrity code)`: the behaviour is in the spec, but the integrity code it checks is defined
   only in the RTL (`tlul_pkg.sv`): [TLUL] "Bus Integrity Scheme" says only "To be filled in."
   Please confirm.
** `RTL`: taken from reading the RTL where the spec is silent. Please confirm. No requirement has
   this source; assumptions A1, A9 and A14-A16 rest partly on the RTL.
* Every requirement and assumption whose Source is not `spec` has a question for the designers
  (designer questions): Q15 and Q18-Q20 for `DV reading`, Q21 for `RTL (integrity code)`,
  Q12 and Q22-Q24 for the assumptions. The other 125 requirements are `spec`.
* Each requirement is checked at the boundary of its checker
  (xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc#checkers[TB architecture, three checkers]).
* Every requirement holds under the assumptions of <<assumptions>>.
  End-to-end requirements that no single checker holds are closed by composition (xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc#composition[End-to-end requirements by composition]).

=== Tag filter

*Scope:* every `REQ_TF_*` covers all core accesses except a capability store to the NVM (a write in
CHERIoT mode to the NVM with the tag sideband set, [ToO] WTRC). Those belong to the WTRC, outside
this plan. The testbench tells them apart from the request alone, so the checks skip exactly
those.

[cols="4,6,5,6,3,4,3,3",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Requirement |Why it matters |Spec ref |Source |Category |Obligations |Status

|`REQ_TF_01a`
|Every core access shall be forwarded to the host port exactly once.
|A dropped access never reaches memory; a duplicate reads or writes twice.
|[ToO] port table, `cored_tl_h`: "The data half of the access, forwarded to SRAM, NVM and
peripherals."
|spec |functional |to plan |gap, raised with the designers

|`REQ_TF_01b`
|A request on the host port shall carry the A-channel fields of the core access it forwards,
unchanged.
|A changed address or data would corrupt ordinary memory traffic.
|[ToO] port table, `cored_tl_h` (as above); [ToO] WTRC: "Every other access passes through the
WTRC unchanged and with unchanged timing"
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TF_01c`
|The host port shall carry no request that the core did not present.
|A request the core never made reads or writes memory behind software's back.
|[ToO] port table, `cored_tl_h` (as above)
|spec |security |to plan |gap, raised with the designers

|`REQ_TF_02`
|In CHERIoT mode, a 64-bit-aligned read hinted as a capability load to a tagged region shall issue
one meta lookup.
|Without the lookup the core never learns the tag; every capability load would fail.
|[ToO] Tag Filter: "A meta lookup is needed when CHERIoT mode is enabled, the access targets memory
capable of holding capabilities, and either: the access is a 64-bit-aligned read that the core
hints as a capability load."; the hint: [CIBEX] `data_tag_o` "When high, the current write transaction carries a valid capability tag or the current load transaction is a capability load."
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TF_03`
|In CHERIoT mode, a write to a tagged region shall issue one meta lookup, except a capability store
to the NVM.
|A store that skips its lookup leaves a stale valid tag next to plain data: a forged capability.
|[ToO] Tag Filter: "the access is a write, of any kind."; "The exception is a capability store to
the NVM ... it is not looked up"
|spec |security |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TF_04`
|No other access shall issue a meta request; in particular none outside CHERIoT mode.
|Extra lookups waste meta SRAM bandwidth; lookups in ePMP mode break the mode gating.
|[ToO] Tag Filter (lookup conditions); [HJSON] `MODE_GATING`: "No tag lookups are issued.";
[HJSON] `INTERSIG.MUBI`: "The CHERIoT mode enable is multi-bit encoded."
|spec |security |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TF_05a`
|A meta request shall address the meta word that holds the tag of the 8-byte location containing
the access address.
|A wrong word reads or changes another capability's tag.
|[ToO] Metadata Encoding table, row "Capability tag": "one 8-byte capability" per bit, "256 bytes
of data" per 32-bit word; [ToO] Meta SRAM Address Map
|spec |functional |to plan |gap, raised with the designers

|`REQ_TF_05b`
|A meta request's bit select shall name that location's bit within the meta word.
|A wrong bit reads or changes a neighbour's tag.
|[ToO] Metadata Encoding (as above)
|spec |functional |to plan |gap, raised with the designers

|`REQ_TF_06`
|A write's meta request shall carry the write's tag sideband as the tag to write.
|A plain store must write 0; a capability store must write the capability's tag.
|[IF] `cored_tag_h2d`: "CHERIoT capability tag carried with the A-channel"; [HJSON]
`TAG_CLEAR_ON_DATA_WRITE`: "Any non-capability write clears the tag bit of the addressed location";
ISA §7.7: the tag bits "may be set to one only by a store of a tagged capability using CSC"
|spec |security |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TF_07`
|Each core response shall carry its request's host response: opcode, size, source, data, data
integrity and, when no meta error is merged in, response integrity.
|A mixed-up response gives the core another request's data.
|[ToO] Tag Filter: "the streams are joined together and the data response is returned to the core"
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TF_08`
|A read response without `d_error` to a request that made a lookup shall carry the tag of its meta
response. An error response's tag is not checked.
|This is how W0 of a capability load gets its tag.
|[ToO] Tag Filter: "on a response whose FIFO entry was marked aligned, the tag read from the meta
SRAM is presented and captured"; on an error "the core will raise an exception" ([LSU]), so it
does not use the tag
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TF_09`
|The next unaligned read response after an aligned one shall carry the captured tag.
|This is how W1 of a capability load gets the same tag without a second lookup.
|[ToO] Tag Filter: "on the following unaligned response the captured value is presented again and
then cleared"; [CIBEX]: "Since Ibex only has a 32-bit interface, it reads and writes capabilities in two consecutive transactions."
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TF_10`
|The captured tag shall be cleared after that unaligned read response.
|A capture left behind would hand a valid tag to a later, unrelated load.
|[ToO] Tag Filter, same sentence: "and then cleared"
|spec |security |to plan |planned: on the core's tag filter a plain read of the upper word right
after the load observes it; on the engine's, when the engine clears a tag

|`REQ_TF_11a`
|A write response shall be untagged.
|A store must never hand the core a valid tag.
|[ToO] Tag Filter: "a write answered between the two words of a capability is returned untagged and
leaves the captured value alone"
|spec |security |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TF_11b`
|A write response shall leave the captured tag unchanged.
|A store answered between W0 and W1 must not reset the load's tag.
|[ToO] Tag Filter (same sentence)
|spec |functional |to plan |out of scope on the core's tag filter: only a write between W0 and W1
reaches it; the engine's tag filter may reach it, when the engine clears a tag

|`REQ_TF_11c`
|A read response shall be untagged unless its request was hinted as a capability load, to a tagged
region, in CHERIoT mode.
|A tag of 1 where no capability was loaded hands the core a valid capability it never stored.
|[CIBEX] `data_tag_i`: "Must be driven high if and only if the loaded word has a stored/valid
capability tag and the request was a capability load."; ISA §7.7: "In memory without tag support
capability stores will silently drop the tag, and capability loads will always return untagged
values."
|spec |security |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TF_12a`
|`d_error` towards the core shall be set when the host response or the joined meta response has an
error.
|A failed tag access hidden from the core would leave software trusting a bad tag.
|[ToO] Tag Filter: "Error responses from either the host or the meta path are merged into `d_error`
towards the core."
|spec |error |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TF_12b`
|`d_error` towards the core shall be clear when neither the host response nor a joined meta
response has an error.
|A false error makes the core take a bus fault on a good access.
|[ToO] Tag Filter (same sentence)
|spec |error |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TF_13`
|When a meta error sets `d_error` on an error-free host response, the response integrity shall be
valid if the host's was valid, and invalid if it was invalid.
|A valid response must not look like a fault; a faulty one must not look valid.
|[ToO] Tag Filter: "a correct integrity stays correct and a broken one stays broken"
|spec + RTL (integrity code) |security |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TF_14`
|The meta port shall always accept a meta response.
|Refusing one can deadlock the two tag filters that share the RMW filter (tf meta accept).
|[ToO] Tag Filter: "so it never refuses a response (`MetaRspAlwaysAccepted_A`). The meta path
therefore never waits for a data response"
|spec |interface |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TF_15a`
|With at most two requests outstanding, the filter shall eventually accept every request, given the
host and meta ports accept.
|A filter that stalls hangs the core.
|[ToO] Tag Filter: "The FIFO depth sets the number of outstanding transactions the filter supports.
It is two for the core's tag filter"
|spec |liveness |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TF_15b`
|The filter shall answer every accepted request exactly once, given the host and meta ports answer.
|A lost answer hangs the core; a second answer is taken for a later request.
|[ToO] Tag Filter (as above); [TLUL]: "All bus devices must simply return the associated
`a_source` on the response `d_source` bus."
|spec |liveness |to plan |gap, raised with the designers

|`REQ_TF_16a`
|A request shall reach the host port, and the meta port if it needs a lookup, in the cycle the
core presents it.
|The spec promises zero latency overhead for reads.
|[ToO] Timing: "a request propagates combinationally from `cored_tl_d` through the tag filter ...
and the response propagates back the same way"
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TF_16b`
|A response shall reach the core in the cycle its last part arrives.
|The same promise, on the way back.
|[ToO] Timing (as above)
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TF_17`
|Every tag lookup the tag filter generates shall carry a valid command integrity.
|A wrong code on a generated request raises the meta SRAM controller's fatal alert on a legal
access.
|[README] Overview: "Requests that the subsystem generates or rewrites get command and data
integrity"; [HJSON] `BUS.INTEGRITY`
|spec |security |to plan |planned
|===

*Questions for the designers* (designer questions): Q2 on `REQ_TF_05a`, `REQ_TF_05b`; Q12 on `REQ_TF_01a`,
`REQ_TF_01c`, `REQ_TF_15b`; Q21 on `REQ_TF_13`; Q24 on `REQ_TF_15a`, `REQ_TF_15b`.

=== 2:1 tag arbiter

*Scope:* every `REQ_ARB_*` covers both inputs, so the TBRE's requests are checked while they pass
the arbiter, whatever the TBRE sends. What the TBRE asks for, and what the tag clear squash does to
its clears, belong to checker 3 (revocation engine). `REQ_ARB_01`-`REQ_ARB_10` are checked at the
arbiter's own ports, `REQ_ARB_11` at the RMW filter's upstream port.

[cols="4,6,5,6,3,4,3,3",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Requirement |Why it matters |Spec ref |Source |Category |Obligations |Status

|`REQ_ARB_01`
|Every request accepted on either input shall be forwarded to the RMW filter exactly once.
|A dropped tag request hangs its tag filter; a duplicate makes a second read-modify-write and a
second answer.
|[ToO] RMW Filter: "a `cheriot_socket_m1` arbitrates their meta ports ... onto the single RMW
filter, so every tag update of the subsystem goes through one read-modify-write."
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_ARB_02`
|No request shall be forwarded that neither input presented.
|An invented request changes a tag nobody wrote.
|[ToO] RMW Filter (as above)
|spec |security |to plan |planned

|`REQ_ARB_03`
|A forwarded request shall carry the A-channel fields of the request it forwards unchanged, except
`a_source`.
|A changed address or opcode reads or writes the wrong tag.
|[ToO] RMW Filter (as above); [TLUL] Source ID requirements for bus primitives: `a_source` is the
field an `M:1` socket changes ("The exception is for `M:1` sockets")
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_ARB_04`
|A forwarded request shall carry the tag and bit select of the request it forwards.
|The other input's bit select changes a neighbour's tag: a forged or a lost capability.
|[ToO] RMW Filter: "carrying the tag and bit select sideband"
|spec |security |to plan |planned

|`REQ_ARB_05`
|Every answer shall go to the input whose request it answers, and to no other.
|An answer at the wrong tag filter leaves one waiting and misleads the other.
|[ToO] RMW Filter: "every answer returns to the tag filter that sent the request"
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_ARB_06`
|An answer shall carry, as `d_source`, the `a_source` its input sent.
|The tag filter matches each answer to its request by this ID.
|[TLUL] Source ID growth: "those ... sub-source bits are shifted off, with `'0'` bits shifted into
the top, and returned to the originator's `d_source`{empty}"
|spec |interface |to plan |planned

|`REQ_ARB_07`
|An answer shall reach its input with every D-channel field except `d_source`, and its tag,
unchanged.
|A changed answer gives a tag filter the wrong tag, or hides an error.
|[ToO] Timing: "the response propagates back the same way"; [ToO] RMW Filter: "carrying the tag
and bit select sideband"
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_ARB_08`
|A request held on either input shall eventually be accepted, given the RMW filter keeps accepting
requests.
|A TBRE sweep must not starve the core's tag requests, or the core hangs.
|[ToO] RMW Filter: "arbitrates their meta ports", with no policy named; [TLUL]
`tlul_socket_m1`: "Requests coming from each host ports are arbitrated in the socket based on
round-robin scheme."
|DV reading |liveness |to plan |gap, raised with the designers

|`REQ_ARB_09`
|A request presented while the other input presents none shall reach the RMW filter in the same
cycle.
|The spec promises zero latency overhead for reads.
|[ToO] Timing: "a request propagates combinationally from `cored_tl_d` through the tag filter, the
`cheriot_socket_m1` in front of the RMW filter, the RMW filter, access checker and arbiter to
`meta_sram_tl`{empty}"
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_ARB_10`
|An answer shall reach its input in the cycle the RMW filter gives it.
|The same promise, on the way back.
|[ToO] Timing (as above): "and the response propagates back the same way"
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_ARB_11`
|A request from the core's tag filter shall reach the RMW filter exactly as the arbiter forwards it.
|The tag clear squash in between may change only the TBRE's stale clears; a changed core write
would write the wrong tag.
|[ToO] Revocation Engine: "a core write to the same capability marks the clear stale, and the RMW
filter then only reads the tag word instead of clearing the tag"; [ToO] Timing names no stage
between the `cheriot_socket_m1` and the RMW filter
|spec |security |to plan |planned
|===

*Questions for the designers* (designer questions): Q15 on `REQ_ARB_08`; Q22 on `REQ_ARB_06`.

=== RMW filter

[cols="4,6,5,6,3,4,3,3",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Requirement |Why it matters |Spec ref |Source |Category |Obligations |Status

|`REQ_RMW_01`
|A read shall be forwarded on the downstream port, towards the meta SRAM, at its meta word
address.
|Reading another word returns another capability's tag.
|[ToO] RMW Filter, `Passthrough`: "A read is forwarded"
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_RMW_02`
|A read's response without `d_error` shall return the bit of the response word its bit select
names as the tag. An error response's tag is not checked.
|The wrong bit is another capability's tag.
|[ToO] RMW Filter, `Passthrough`: "the tag bit is picked out of the response word"; the core does
not use an error response's tag ([LSU], see `REQ_TF_08`)
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_RMW_03`
|A write shall first issue a full-word `Get` of its meta word on the downstream port.
|The other 31 tags of the word must be known before the word is rewritten.
|[ToO] RMW Filter, `Passthrough`: "A write is turned into a `Get` of the meta word"
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_RMW_04`
|A write whose tag equals the stored bit shall issue no write-back.
|Keeps the shared meta SRAM free in the common case.
|[ToO] RMW Filter, `Fill`: "If the stored tag bit already equals the tag to be written"
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_RMW_05`
|A write with no write-back shall be answered with an `AccessAck`.
|The requester waits for an answer to every write.
|[ToO] RMW Filter, `Fill`: "the read response is converted into an `AccessAck` towards the core"
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_RMW_06`
|A write whose tag differs from the stored bit shall write back the read word with that bit set to
the tag and every other bit unchanged.
|Changing any other bit forges or destroys another capability's tag.
|[ToO] RMW Filter, `Fill`: "the word is captured, the bit is modified, and the FSM advances"
|spec |security |to plan |planned

|`REQ_RMW_07`
|The write-back shall be a full-word `PutFullData` to the same meta word, with freshly computed
command and data integrity.
|The access checker refuses anything else; stale integrity would raise a false fault.
|[ToO] RMW Filter, `WriteBackReq`: "The modified word is written back with `PutFullData` and
freshly computed command and data integrity."
|spec + RTL (integrity code) |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_RMW_08`
|The write-back's response shall be forwarded as the write's response.
|The requester must learn whether the tag write succeeded.
|[ToO] RMW Filter, `WriteBackAck`: "The write response is forwarded to the core"
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_RMW_09`
|Every request issued for a write shall carry the write's `a_source`.
|The answer must find its way back to the tag filter that asked.
|[ToO] RMW Filter: "The meta SRAM reads and writes it issues for a write carry the requester's
`a_source`{empty}"
|spec |interface |to plan |planned

|`REQ_RMW_10`
|A new request shall be accepted only in a cycle in which no earlier operation is unanswered, or in
which the only unanswered operation is a read answered in that cycle.
|A request taken mid-operation would overwrite the stored address, bit or tag and lose a tag write.
|[ToO] RMW Filter: "it takes a new request only while no operation is unanswered, or in the cycle a
read is answered"
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_RMW_11`
|A read presented in the cycle the previous read is answered shall be accepted in that cycle, if the
downstream port is ready.
|Capability loads must not be slowed down by the RMW filter.
|[ToO] RMW Filter: "This keeps back-to-back reads at one per cycle"
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_RMW_13`
|A device error on the `Get` of a write shall abort the write: no write-back.
|Writing back a word that was never read correctly could corrupt 31 other tags.
|[ToO] Error Handling, row "Device error on the tag path": "Read-modify-write aborted, `d_error`
towards the core, and `fatal_fault` alert"
|spec |error |to plan |planned

|`REQ_RMW_14`
|A device error on a meta SRAM response shall be answered upstream with `d_error`.
|The core must learn that its tag access failed; the alert is `REQ_TAG_07`.
|[ToO] Error Handling, row "Device error on the tag path" (as `REQ_RMW_13`)
|spec |error |to plan |planned

|`REQ_RMW_15`
|Every accepted request shall be answered once, given the meta SRAM answers.
|A lost answer hangs a tag filter, and with it the core.
|[TLUL]: "All bus devices must simply return the associated `a_source` on the response `d_source`
bus."; [ToO] RMW Filter state table: every state returns to `Passthrough` with a response
|spec |liveness |to plan |planned

|`REQ_RMW_16`
|The downstream port shall carry no request other than one `Get` of the meta word per accepted
request and, for a write whose tag differs from the stored bit, one `PutFullData` write-back.
|A request the filter invents, such as a write-back for a read, changes a tag nobody wrote.
|[ToO] RMW Filter, `Passthrough`: "A read is forwarded"; "A write is turned into a `Get` of the meta
word"; [ToO] RMW Filter: "it costs one meta SRAM read per 32-bit store, and a read plus a write only
when the tag actually changes"
|spec |security |to plan |planned

|`REQ_RMW_17`
|`d_error` upstream shall be clear when neither the `Get` answer nor the write-back answer of the
operation has a device error.
|A false error makes the core take a bus fault on a good tag access, and fails the engine's clear.
|[ToO] RMW Filter: `Passthrough`, "A read is forwarded"; `Fill`, "the read response is converted
into an `AccessAck` towards the core"; `WriteBackAck`, "The write response is forwarded to the
core"; [ToO] Error Handling names no other cause of `d_error` at the RMW filter
|spec |error |to plan |planned

|`REQ_RMW_18`
|The `Get` the RMW filter generates for a read or for a write shall carry a valid command
integrity.
|A wrong code on a generated request raises the meta SRAM controller's fatal alert on a legal
access.
|[README] Overview: "Requests that the subsystem generates or rewrites get command and data
integrity"; [HJSON] `BUS.INTEGRITY`
|spec |security |to plan |planned
|===

*Questions for the designers* (designer questions): Q21 on `REQ_RMW_07`; Q24 on `REQ_RMW_15`;
Q43 on `REQ_RMW_06`.

*Scope of `REQ_RMW_04`-`REQ_RMW_09`, `REQ_RMW_14`, `REQ_RMW_16` and `REQ_RMW_17`:* when the `Get`
of a write is answered with no `d_error` and a broken response or data integrity, [ToO] Error
Handling raises `fatal_fault` and says nothing more. No requirement claims whether the write-back follows or how
often, what it carries (its `a_source` too) or how the write is answered (its `d_error` too): the
alert stays raised until reset (`REQ_TAG_10`), so no requirement claims the case
(xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_tag_path_uarch.adoc#decisions_made[checker 1 uarch, D62]).
The end-to-end rows composed from these requirements inherit the limit: `REQ_TAG_01`-`REQ_TAG_04`
and `REQ_TBRE_38` hold until such an answer (<<tag_end_to_end>>, Scope). The RTL does write back a
word computed from the corrupt data when the requested bit differs (`cheriot_rmw_filter.sv`, the
skip condition has no integrity term; information only), so question Q43 asks whether the
write-back should be aborted.

'''

[[tag_end_to_end]]
=== Tag path end to end

[cols="4,6,5,6,3,4,3,3",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Requirement |Why it matters |Spec ref |Source |Category |Obligations |Status

|`REQ_TAG_01`
|A hinted capability load in CHERIoT mode shall return the tag most recently written to that
capability through the tag path: in the order tag writes reach the meta SRAM, a write aborted by an
error writing nothing, and a capability never written returning the meta SRAM's starting content.
|This is the tag path's purpose: a tag reads back as it was last written.
|[HJSON] `TAG_READ`: "On a hinted capability load, the tag bit of the addressed capability is
looked up in the meta SRAM and returned."; `TAG_SPLIT`: "Their responses are joined so that data
and tag are returned together."
|spec |functional |by composition (xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc#composition[End-to-end requirements by composition]) |planned

|`REQ_TAG_02`
|A write to the main SRAM in CHERIoT mode shall set the addressed capability's tag to the write's
tag sideband, so a non-capability write clears it.
|The rule that stops software from forging capabilities (2.1).
|[HJSON] `TAG_CLEAR_ON_DATA_WRITE`: "Any non-capability write clears the tag bit of the addressed
location, so that data stores cannot modify a valid capability."; ISA §7.7: "non-capability
stores (e.g. CSW) clear the tag bits"
|spec |security |by composition (xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc#composition[End-to-end requirements by composition]) |planned

|`REQ_TAG_03`
|A plain store or an untagged capability store to the NVM shall clear the addressed capability's
tag.
|The same rule for capabilities held in the NVM.
|[PG] Storing Capabilities in the NVM: "A plain store to the NVM, or a `csc` of an untagged
capability, is refused by the NVM and clears the tag of the capability it targets."
|spec |security |by composition (xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc#composition[End-to-end requirements by composition]) |planned

|`REQ_TAG_04`
|A tag write shall change no other capability's tag.
|32 capabilities share a meta word; touching a neighbour forges or destroys its tag.
|[HJSON] `TAG_WRITE_RMW`: "a write performs a read-modify-write on the addressed meta SRAM word"
|spec |security |by composition (xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc#composition[End-to-end requirements by composition]) |planned

|`REQ_TAG_05`
|Tag path accesses shall reach only the capability tag regions of the meta SRAM.
|The tag path must not read or write the revocation bitmap.
|[ToO] Access Checkers: "an access checker parameterized with the region it owns"; [RFC] "the RMW
filter only the tag sections"
|spec |security |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TAG_06`
|Outside CHERIoT mode, no tag path access shall reach the meta SRAM.
|ePMP mode must not depend on, or change, CHERIoT state.
|[ToO] Access Checkers: "any `cheriot_ena_i` value other than a strict `MuBi4True` ... makes the
entire meta SRAM inaccessible from all four ports"; [HJSON] `INTERSIG.MUBI`: "The CHERIoT mode
enable is multi-bit encoded."
|spec |security |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TAG_07`
|A device error on the tag path shall raise `fatal_fault`.
|A broken tag store must stop the chip, not be ignored.
|[ToO] Error Handling, row "Device error on the tag path" (as `REQ_RMW_13`)
|spec |error |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TAG_08`
|An integrity fault on a meta SRAM response to the tag path shall raise `fatal_fault`.
|Fault injection on the tag store must be detected.
|[ToO] Error Handling, row "Integrity fault on a meta SRAM response (`rsp_intg` or `data_intg`)":
its result is a `fatal_fault` alert
|spec + RTL (integrity code) |security |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TAG_09`
|Every core request shall be answered, whatever requests the TBRE's tag filter makes on the shared
RMW filter, given `xbar_main` and the meta SRAM answer.
|The deadlock of tf meta accept must be impossible.
|[ToO] Tag Filter: "a meta response held until its data response arrives could wait on a data
response that is itself queued behind the other tag filter's"
|spec |liveness |by composition (xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc#composition[End-to-end requirements by composition]) |gap, raised with the designers

|`REQ_TAG_10`
|Once raised, `fatal_fault` shall stay raised until reset.
|An alert that clears itself can be missed; a damaged tag store must stay flagged.
|[ToO] Error Handling: "The others latch the fatal alert until reset"
|spec |security |to plan |planned

|`REQ_TAG_11`
|No meta SRAM request from the other three ports shall reach a capability tag region.
|Only the RMW filter may write tags; a second writer would break its read-modify-write.
|[ToO] Meta SRAM Address Map: both capability tag regions are "Reachable from" the "RMW filter"
only
|spec |security |to plan |planned
|===

*Questions for the designers* (designer questions): Q15 and Q24 on `REQ_TAG_09`; Q21 on `REQ_TAG_08`;
Q43 on `REQ_TAG_04`; Q45 on `REQ_TAG_11`.

*Scope of `REQ_TAG_01`-`REQ_TAG_04`:* they hold from reset until the `Get` of a tag write is
answered with no `d_error` and a broken response or data integrity (the RMW filter's Scope,
above): from that answer on, only `REQ_TAG_10` is claimed, and question Q43 asks whether such a
write-back should be aborted. Their composition carries the same premise
(xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc#composition[End-to-end requirements by composition]).

[[meta_access_reqs]]
=== Meta SRAM access

*Scope:* the four access checkers, the 4:1 arbiter (`tlul_socket_m1`) and the revocation bitmap
window, checked at the four requester ports and at `meta_sram_tl` (checker 2, meta access).
`REQ_TAG_05`, `REQ_TAG_06` and `REQ_TAG_11` are the tag path's part of these rules and keep their
IDs.

*Terms:*

* *Requester ports:* the tag port (from the RMW filter), `corerevbm_tl` (the core's TRVK),
  `revbm_tl_d` (software, through `xbar_main`) and the TBRE's TRVK port.
* *Region of a port* ([ToO] Meta SRAM Address Map, "Reachable from"): the tag port owns both
  capability tag regions, `0x1100_0C00`-`0x1100_97FF`; the other three own the revocation bitmap,
  `0x1100_0000`-`0x1100_0BFF`.
* *Legal request:* all four conditions of [ToO] Access Checkers hold: `cheriot_ena_i` is
  `MuBi4True`; the address lies in the port's region; the access is a full 32-bit word at a
  word-aligned address (`a_size` = 2, so TL-UL sets all four `a_mask` bits: [TLUL] protocol
  checker, `sizeMatchesMask`); the opcode is `Get` or `PutFullData`.

[cols="4,6,5,6,3,4,3,3",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Requirement |Why it matters |Spec ref |Source |Category |Obligations |Status

|`REQ_META_01`
|A legal request on a requester port shall be forwarded to `meta_sram_tl` exactly once.
|A dropped request hangs its requester; a duplicate reads or writes the meta SRAM twice.
|[ToO] Access Checkers: "Everything else is steered to a `tlul_err_resp` instance and answered with
a TL-UL error."; [ToO] Arbitration: "A `tlul_socket_m1` arbitrates the four checked streams onto
`meta_sram_tl`."
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_META_02`
|A forwarded request shall carry the A-channel fields of the request it forwards unchanged, except
`a_source`.
|A changed address or data reads or writes the wrong meta word.
|[ToO] Arbitration: "Arbitration sits behind the checkers, on transactions that are already
integrity-protected end to end."; [TLUL] Source ID growth: `a_source` is the field an `M:1` socket
changes
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_META_03`
|No request outside its port's region shall reach `meta_sram_tl`.
|Each port must stay in its own table: a bitmap port that reached a tag word could read or forge a
tag.
|[ToO] Access Checkers: "The address is inside the allowable region for the requester."; [HJSON]
`ACCESS_CHECK`: "Every meta SRAM access is checked against the region and the operations permitted
for its originating port."; [HJSON] `MEM.SW_NOACCESS`: "The capability tag store is not memory
mapped."
|spec |security |to plan |planned

|`REQ_META_04`
|Outside CHERIoT mode, with `cheriot_ena_i` at any value other than `MuBi4True`, no request from
any requester port shall reach `meta_sram_tl`.
|ePMP mode must not read or change CHERIoT state, and one flipped bit of the enable must not open
the meta SRAM.
|[ToO] Access Checkers: "any `cheriot_ena_i` value other than a strict `MuBi4True` - including a
strict `MuBi4False` - makes the entire meta SRAM inaccessible from all four ports"; [HJSON]
`MODE_GATING`; [HJSON] `INTERSIG.MUBI`: "The CHERIoT mode enable is multi-bit encoded."
|spec |security |to plan |planned

|`REQ_META_05`
|No request that is not a full 32-bit word at a word-aligned address shall reach `meta_sram_tl`.
|Only whole words of 32 tags or 32 revocation bits are defined; a sub-word access sees or changes
part of one.
|[ToO] Access Checkers: "The address is word-aligned and the access is a full 32-bit word."
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_META_06`
|No request whose opcode is not `Get` or `PutFullData` shall reach `meta_sram_tl`.
|Software's byte store to the bitmap must fail visibly, not change part of a word.
|[ToO] Access Checkers: "The opcode is `Get` or `PutFullData`."; [ToO] Error Handling, row
`PutPartialData` to the meta SRAM: "TL-UL error response"
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_META_07`
|A request that is not legal shall be answered once, with `d_error` set.
|The requester must learn that its access was refused, or it waits for ever.
|[ToO] Access Checkers (as `REQ_META_01`); [ToO] Error Handling: the rows for a meta SRAM access in
ePMP mode, an access outside the requester's region and `PutPartialData`, each "TL-UL error
response"
|spec |error |to plan |planned

|`REQ_META_08`
|No request shall reach `meta_sram_tl` that no requester port presented.
|An invented request reads or writes a meta word nobody asked for.
|[ToO] Arbitration (as `REQ_META_01`)
|spec |security |to plan |planned

|`REQ_META_09`
|Every answer from `meta_sram_tl` shall go to the requester port whose request it answers, and to no
other.
|An answer at the wrong port leaves one requester waiting and misleads another.
|[TLUL] Source ID growth: "those ... sub-source bits are shifted off, with `'0'` bits shifted into
the top, and returned to the originator's `d_source`{empty}"
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_META_10`
|An answer shall carry, as `d_source`, the `a_source` its requester sent.
|Each requester matches an answer to its request by this ID.
|[TLUL]: "All bus devices must simply return the associated `a_source` on the response `d_source`
bus."
|spec |interface |to plan |planned

|`REQ_META_11`
|An answer shall reach its requester with every D-channel field except `d_source` unchanged.
|A changed answer gives a requester the wrong word, or hides an error.
|[ToO] Timing: "the response propagates back the same way"; [ToO] Arbitration: "transactions that
are already integrity-protected end to end"
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_META_12`
|A request held on a requester port shall eventually be accepted, given the meta SRAM keeps
accepting requests.
|A busy requester, such as a TBRE sweep, must not starve the others.
|[TLUL] `tlul_socket_m1`: "Requests coming from each host ports are arbitrated in the socket based
on round-robin scheme."
|spec |liveness |to plan |CEX

|`REQ_META_13`
|Every accepted request shall be answered exactly once, given the meta SRAM answers and every
requester takes its answers.
|A lost answer hangs its requester; a second one is taken for a later request.
|[TLUL]: "All bus devices must simply return the associated `a_source` on the response `d_source`
bus."
|spec |liveness |to plan |CEX

|`REQ_META_14`
|A legal request presented while no other requester port presents one shall reach `meta_sram_tl`
in the same cycle.
|The spec promises zero latency overhead for reads.
|[ToO] Timing: "All internal sockets and the socket towards the meta SRAM are instantiated with
zero-depth FIFOs"
|spec |functional |to plan |CEX

|`REQ_META_15`
|An answer from `meta_sram_tl` shall reach its requester in the cycle it arrives.
|The same promise, on the way back.
|[ToO] Timing: "the response propagates back the same way"
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_META_16`
|An access checker's error answer shall carry a valid response integrity and, for a `Get`, a
valid data integrity.
|A denial software can cause would otherwise become an integrity fault at the requester.
|[TLUL] Usage of User Bits: the response integrity "is checked by the transaction originator";
[README] Overview: "Requests that the subsystem generates or rewrites get command and data
integrity"
|spec |security |to plan |planned
|===

*Questions for the designers* (designer questions): Q22 on `REQ_META_10`; Q24 on `REQ_META_12`, `REQ_META_13`;
Q45 on `REQ_META_03`-`REQ_META_07`; Q48 on `REQ_META_04`, `REQ_META_07`.

'''

[[wtrc_reqs]]
=== WTRC

*Scope:* a *capability store to the NVM*, "a write in strict CHERIoT mode to the NVM with the tag
sideband set" ([ToO] WTRC), and the requests around it. Its two words are W0 (address bit 2 = 0)
and W1 (bit 2 = 1). Every other access passes the WTRC and is covered by the `REQ_TF_*` rows,
checked with the WTRC in place. The core never sends a store out of sequence or a tagged
partial store (A4, A5); the rows on those cases check the WTRC's reaction in a run without A4 and
A5 for the NVM (xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc#run_variants[testplan, run
variants]).

*Terms* ([ToO] WTRC):

* *Out of sequence:* with no capability open, a W1; with W0 taken, anything but the W1 of the same
  capability; with W1 taken but neither answered nor turned into a tag write, a W1 or any request;
  with W1's tag write issued, a W1, or a W0 before W1 is answered. "A W0 taken always opens a
  capability, and W1's answer closes it; the next W0 may be taken in the cycle W1 is answered."
* *Matched:* the word's NVM read succeeded, the word is a full-word `PutFullData` in sequence, and
  its data and data integrity equal the NVM's (row W0 of the [ToO] WTRC table).

[cols="4,6,5,6,3,4,3,3",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Requirement |Why it matters |Spec ref |Source |Category |Obligations |Status

|`REQ_WTRC_01`
|A capability store to the NVM shall reach the host port only as a `Get` of the word it targets,
never as a write.
|The store is verified by reading the word; a write would reach the NVM instead of the compare.
|[ToO] WTRC: "is not written: it is turned into a `Get` of the word it targets"
|spec |functional |to plan |planned

|`REQ_WTRC_02`
|That `Get` shall carry a valid command integrity.
|The store's own integrity covers a `PutFullData`; on a `Get` it would be a false integrity fault.
|[ToO] WTRC: "with recomputed command integrity"
|spec + RTL (integrity code) |interface |to plan |planned

|`REQ_WTRC_03`
|A capability store to the NVM shall issue no lookup: W0 no meta request, W1 none but its tag write
(`REQ_WTRC_06`).
|A lookup would write the tag before the store is verified: a capability the NVM does not hold would
become valid.
|[ToO] WTRC: "It does no lookup."; [ToO] Tag Filter: "only its second word writes the tag, once the
store is verified"
|spec |security |to plan |planned

|`REQ_WTRC_04a`
|W0 shall be answered with `d_error` if its NVM read failed, it is not a full-word `PutFullData`, it
is out of sequence, or its data or data integrity differ from the NVM's.
|Software must learn that the capability store failed.
|[ToO] WTRC table, row W0: "``AccessAck``; `d_error` if the NVM read failed, the store is not a

cannot produce"
|spec + RTL (integrity code) |security |to plan |CEX on the integrity faults; out of scope for

|`REQ_WTRC_13`
|Every access that is not a capability store to the NVM shall pass the WTRC unchanged and with

[[tbre_reqs]]
=== Revocation engine

*Scope:* the TBRE (background revocation engine), its sweep control and registers, the core write
watch and the tag clear squash, checked in checker 3. The capability's base, sealing state and
revocation bit are defined below, from the ISA (<<capability_terms,capability terms>>); the testplan holds the
formulas (xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc#defs_capability[testplan,
Definitions]).

[[capability_terms]]
*Capability terms* (ISA):

* *Base* of a capability: the lowest address it covers, decoded from its address and its bounds
  fields. ISA §7.13.3 (PDF pages 69-70): "The capability bounds (base and top) are stored in a
  compressed format relative to the address".
* *Sealing capability:* a capability whose permissions are in the sealing format and grant SE, US
  or U0, the capabilities CLC exempts: `isSealingCap = cr.permit_seal | cr.permit_unseal |
  cr.perm_user0` (ISA, CLC, PDF page 114). ISA §7.8 (PDF page 58): "The base of sealing
  capabilities (see Figure 7.4) refers to a distinct namespace to that of memory capabilities,
  therefore they are not revoked using this mechanism." A capability with no permissions: Q17.
* *Revocation bit of a base:* "There is one revocation bit for every 8 bytes." (ISA §9.2, PDF page
  88). The engine uses the bit of the capability's base, not its address: [ToO] "whose base has its
  revocation bit set"; ISA §7.8 (PDF page 58): CLC "loads the revocation bit corresponding to the
  base address of the capability". It is bit `b` of bitmap word `w`, with `w * 32 + b` = (base −
  `MainSramBaseAddr`) / 8 ([ToO] Meta SRAM Address Map). Example: base `0x1000_4000` is word 64,
  bit 0 (revocation).

*Terms* ([ToO] Revocation Engine, [PG], [HJSON]):

* *Taken start:* a write of 1 to `TBRE_START` while `TBRE_REGWEN` is 1, in CHERIoT mode, with
  `TBRE_NUM_CAPS` not zero and `TBRE_BASE_ADDR` in a tagged region. Any other write of 1 to
  `TBRE_START` while `TBRE_REGWEN` is 1 is an *ignored start*. BASE and NUM are the values of
  `TBRE_BASE_ADDR` and `TBRE_NUM_CAPS` at the start.
* *Swept capabilities:* the N capabilities at BASE, BASE + 8, ..., with N = min(NUM, (top − BASE)
  / 8) and top the `MainSramTopAddr` or `NvmTopAddr` of BASE's region.
* *Active:* `TBRE_REGWEN` is 0.
* *Revoked:* a swept capability whose tag is set, which is not a sealing capability, whose base lies
  in the main SRAM region, and whose base's revocation bit is set or whose bitmap lookup failed.
* *Watch window* of a capability: from the presentation of the read of its lower word until its
  clear is presented ([ToO]: "The watch starts when the engine presents the read of the capability's
  lower word, and a capability written from then on until its clear is presented is not
  cleared.").
* A core write *touches* a capability when it is presented on `cored_tl_d`, or accepted there and
  not yet answered, with its address in the capability's 8 bytes ([ToO]: "every write the core
  presents on `cored_tl_d`, and every write it accepted there until the write is answered"; "at
  capability granularity").

[[alert_reqs]]
=== Registers and alert

*Scope:* the register file and the `fatal_fault` alert. The register file is a blackbox in checker
3, so its requirements are checked by the CSR testing; the alert is checked by composition where an
alert cause sits in another checker. The alert causes of the tag path, the WTRC and the engine are
rows of their own groups (`REQ_TAG_07`, `REQ_TAG_08`, `REQ_WTRC_11`, `REQ_WTRC_12`, `REQ_TBRE_33` to
`REQ_TBRE_35`); `REQ_TAG_10` keeps the alert raised until reset.

[cols="4,6,5,6,3,4,3,3",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Requirement |Why it matters |Spec ref |Source |Category |Obligations |Status

|`REQ_REG_01`
|Every register field shall reset to its reset value and behave as its access type, as [HJSON]
and `doc/registers.md` define them.
|Software relies on the documented register behaviour.
|[HJSON] registers; `doc/registers.md`
|spec |configuration |CSR testing (`csr`), for example the bound `csr_assert_fpv` |planned

|`REQ_REG_02`
|The register interface shall take a request at most every other cycle.
|A read right after a start must already see the sweep (`REQ_TBRE_12`).
|[ToO] Revocation Engine: "The register interface takes a request at most every other cycle, so a
read issued right after a start already sees the sweep in both."
|spec |interface |register-file unit (`csr`) |planned

|`REQ_ALT_01`
|An integrity fault on a request on `regs_tl_d` shall raise `fatal_fault`.
|A tampered register write must stop the chip, not reach the engine.
|[ToO] Error Handling: "Integrity fault on the CSR interface \| `fatal_fault` alert"
|spec + RTL (integrity code) |security |CSR testing (`csr`) |planned

|`REQ_ALT_02`
|A write of 1 to `ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault` while `ALERT_TEST.regwen` is 1 shall request one
`fatal_fault` alert.
|Software must be able to test the alert path.
|`doc/registers.md` `ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault`: "Write 1 to trigger one alert event of this kind."
|spec |functional |CSR testing (`alert_test`) |planned

|`REQ_ALT_03`
|Once software writes 0 to `ALERT_TEST.regwen`, it shall read 0, and writes to
`ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault` shall request no alert, until reset.
|Locked alert testing stops later software from faking a fatal alert.
|`doc/registers.md` `ALERT_TEST.regwen`: "Write 0 to disable alert testing until the next reset.";
`rw0c`
|spec |security |common alert test (`alert_test`) |planned

|`REQ_ALT_04`
|A meta SRAM access in ePMP mode, an access outside its port's region and a `PutPartialData` to the
meta SRAM shall raise no alert.
|Software can cause all three; an alert would let software stop the chip.
|[ToO] Error Handling: "The first three ... are reachable by software and surface as a bus fault in
the core ... none of them raises an alert."
|spec |security |by composition (checkers 1, 2, 3) |planned

|`REQ_ALT_05`
|`fatal_fault` shall be requested only for a cause [ToO] Error Handling lists, or by
`ALERT_TEST`.
|A false fatal alert stops a working chip.
|[ToO] Error Handling; [IF] `fatal_fault`: "This fatal alert is triggered when ..."
|spec |security |by composition (checkers 1, 3, the CSR testing) |planned
|===

*Questions for the designers* (designer questions): Q21 on `REQ_ALT_01`.

'''

[[assumptions]]
=== Assumptions

*Rule:* the requirements hold only under these assumptions about the subsystem's inputs and
neighbours. An assumption the design does not really get would hide bugs, so please check each
row against your design. The FPV environment implements them
(xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc#env_tag_path[TB architecture, FPV environment]).

[cols="1,6,5,6,2",options="header"]
|===
|ID |We assume |Why DV needs it |Basis |Source

|A1
|The core keeps a request on `cored_tl_d`, with its tag sideband, unchanged until the subsystem
accepts it, while the life-cycle controller enables the CPU.
|A request that changes while the tag filter forks it leaves the fork half done: the host port
took one request, the meta port another.
|gap, raised with the designers. [LSU]: `data_req_o` "must stay high until `data_gnt_i` is high for one cycle"
|spec + RTL

|A2
|The core has at most two requests outstanding: it presents a new request only while fewer than
two are outstanding, or in the cycle one is answered.
|The metadata FIFO has two entries (tf fifo); a third outstanding request is a case the core
never creates.
|[ToO] Tag Filter: "Ibex's LSU, which never issues more than two outstanding split-access halves"
|spec

|A3
|A capability load is a hinted read of W0 (address bit 2 = 0), followed as the next request by a
hinted read of W0 + 4 (W1), each a full-word read (`a_size` 2). A hinted read with address bit 2 =
1 comes only as that W1.
|A request between W0 and W1, or a W1 alone, would take or leave the captured tag
(tf sticky).
|[CIBEX]: "Since Ibex only has a 32-bit interface, it reads and writes capabilities in two
consecutive transactions."; [LSU] `data_tag_o`: "Also driven high on both beats of a capability
load to request tag data from memory."; answered by the designers
|spec

|A4
|A capability store to the NVM is W0, then W1, and the core sends nothing else until W1 is
answered.
|The WTRC, kept in the tag path as it is, would see sequences the core never sends.
|[ToO] WTRC: "The core stores a capability as two words, W0 at the lower and then W1 at the upper
address, and issues nothing else until W1 is answered."
|spec

|A5
|A partial write (`PutPartialData`) from the core carries tag sideband 0.
|A byte store with tag 1 would set a tag, which no core store does.
|ISA §7.7: the tag bits "may be set to one only by a store of a tagged capability using CSC"; the
core is the only host on `cored_tl_d` ([ToO] Block Diagram); answered by the designers
|spec

|A6
|`cheriot_ena_i` keeps one value from reset. DV checks each value, CHERIoT mode and ePMP mode, but
not the switch between them.
|A mode switch with a tag access in flight is a case the system never creates.
|[ToO] Block Diagram: "driven by the write-once mode switch in `rv_core_ibex`{empty}"; answered by the designers:
when the mode switches, the core's only outstanding access is its `CHERIOT_LOCK` write, outside
both tagged regions, and the TBRE is idle
|spec

|A7
|`xbar_main` answers the subsystem's data requests on `cored_tl_h` in request order.
|The tag filter pairs each answer with its oldest metadata FIFO entry; an answer out of order
would get another request's tag.
|[LSU] Protocol: "it is assumed that the memory requests will be kept in-order"; answered by the designers
|spec

|A8
|The blocks outside the subsystem follow the TL-UL handshake rules: the core and the core's TRVK as
hosts; `xbar_main` as device on `cored_tl_h` and as host on `revbm_tl_d`; the meta SRAM as device,
with one answer per accepted request and `d_source` equal to its `a_source`.
|Without them the checks would see handshakes and answers no real block makes.
|[TLUL]: "All bus devices must simply return the associated `a_source` on the response `d_source`
bus."; the subsystem's own ports are checked against the same rules
|spec

|A9
|Requesters leave the top bits of `a_source` free for the bits the arbiters add: three bits on the
tag path (the core's and the TBRE's tag requests: one bit at the 2:1 tag arbiter, two at the 4:1
arbiter), two bits on the other three meta SRAM ports.
|An arbiter shifts `a_source` left to add its bits. A top bit in use is pushed out, and the answer
comes back to the wrong request.
|[TLUL] Source ID requirements for host elements: "hosts may only use the low bits of the
identifier and cannot assume the entire `AIW` bits will be returned intact"; [TLUL] Source ID
growth (arb)
|spec + RTL

|A10
|`xbar_main` and the meta SRAM eventually answer every request, and the hosts outside the
subsystem (the core's TRVK on `corerevbm_tl`, `xbar_main` on `revbm_tl_d`) eventually take their
answers. Only the "never hangs" requirements need this.
|Without it a neighbour that stalls for ever would fail `REQ_TF_15a`, `REQ_TF_15b`, `REQ_RMW_15`
and `REQ_TAG_09` for a reason outside the subsystem.
|[TL] §5 Deadlock freedom, rule 3 (p29): agents "must eventually accept a presented beat" and
"must eventually answer a received request message". [TLUL] does not restate the rule, so Q24
asks whether OpenTitan's TL-UL keeps it
|spec

|A11
|The meta SRAM returns, for a read, the word last written to that address.
|`REQ_TAG_01`-`REQ_TAG_04` follow from the tag path's checks only if the memory keeps what it is
given; DV does not model the memory.
|Premise P1, verified by the meta SRAM controller's (`sram_ctrl`) own verification; [IF]
`meta_sram_tl`: "Host TL-UL port to the external meta SRAM controller's RAM interface"
|premise

|A12
|`xbar_main` answers the engine's reads on `tbre_tl_h` in request order.
|The engine's tag filter pairs each answer with its oldest metadata FIFO entry, as the core's does
(A7); an answer out of order would get another word's tag.
|*Please confirm: Q23.* [TLUL] `tlul_socket_1n`: "This ensures that all transactions are returned in
order. This feature is still in discussion." [ToO] Tag Filter speaks of "the same in-order SRAMs",
but a sweep of the main SRAM region can read both SRAMs. Unlike A7, no requirement of the
requester backs it ([LSU] covers the core only).
|DV reading

|A13
|`xbar_main` follows the TL-UL handshake rules on the engine's and the registers' ports: as device
on `tbre_tl_h`, as host on `regs_tl_d`.
|Without them the revocation engine's checks would see handshakes and answers no real block makes.
|[TLUL]; as A8 for the other ports
|spec

|A14
|`xbar_main` answers a request on `cored_tl_h` in a later cycle than the one it takes it in.
|An answer in the same cycle reaches the WTRC before its expect FIFO holds the request: a capability
store is answered `AccessAckData`, and later answers are paired with the wrong request.
|*Please confirm: R17.* [TLPC] allows an answer "within the same cycle as the request message is
accepted"; [ToO] does not say how soon `xbar_main` answers. Found in checker 1's first runs,
 `top_earlgrey` keeps it: its crossbar and adapters never answer in the cycle of the
request (R17, In `top_earlgrey`)
|spec + RTL

|A15
|`xbar_main` holds an answer on `cored_tl_h`, unchanged, until the subsystem takes it.
|The WTRC holds W1's NVM answer while it sends the tag write; an answer that changes meanwhile
withdraws the tag write and lets a lookup in first.
|*Please confirm: R18.* [TLUL] has no rule that an answer waits unchanged; OpenTitan's
`tlul_assert` covers "d_valid is dropped" as a legal case. As A1 for the core's requests.
`top_earlgrey` keeps it: every answer comes out of a FIFO or a flop (R18, In `top_earlgrey`)
|spec + RTL

|A16
|The meta SRAM answers on `meta_sram_tl` in a later cycle than the one it takes a request in, in
request order, and holds each answer unchanged until the subsystem takes it.
|The path from the RMW filter to `meta_sram_tl` is combinational ([ToO] Timing), so the RMW filter
sees the meta SRAM's own timing. It pairs an answer with its one operation and reads an answer it
has not taken yet: an answer in the same cycle, out of order, or changing while it waits is
paired with the wrong operation or changes the tag returned.
|*Please confirm: R18.* [IF] `meta_sram_tl`: "Host TL-UL port to the external meta SRAM
controller's RAM interface"; the controller's timing is outside the spec sources (A11, P1).
`top_earlgrey` keeps it: `sram_ctrl_meta` answers through `tlul_adapter_sram` (R18, In
`top_earlgrey`)
|spec + RTL
|===

* *Source* as for the requirements (Source legend), plus `premise`: verified
  elsewhere (A11). `spec + RTL`: A1 rests on the RTL for the path from the core to `cored_tl_d`
, A9 for the tag filter passing the core's `a_source` to its meta port
  (`cheriot_tag_filter.sv` L366), A14-A16 on the RTL of `top_earlgrey`{empty}'s crossbar and
  adapters, with R17 and R18 still asking the designers for a spec rule. `DV reading`: A12;
  A10 rests on [TL] §5 rule 3.
* *Questions for the designers* (designer questions): Q12 on A1; Q48 on A6; Q22 on A9; Q24 on A10; Q23 on
  A12.
* *Not assumed, so the checks cover them:* every address, opcode, size, mask, data value and tag
  sideband TL-UL allows, except A5; every `d_error`; every integrity value, broken ones included;
  any meta word content; reset at any time.
* *Inside the subsystem,* DV also relies on contracts C1-C7 between its own checkers. DV proves each
  one, so they need nothing from you
  (xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc#contracts[TB architecture, Contracts]).
* *Software rules* DV assumes for revocation: findings feed verification.

=== Testpoints

A testpoint groups the requirements one set of checks covers. Each becomes a testpoint of the
testplan hjson when implemented; its result is the result of every check in it.

The testpoints are in the xref:../testplan/cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_testplan.adoc[FPV testplan]: 42
testpoints over the 144 requirements, each requirement in exactly one, with the rule as a formula,
the cases and edge cases the tool must reach, what must never happen, and the run that checks it.
